title: Second-highest coefficient of the chromatic polynomial
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex set $V$, with $\nu = |V|$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges, and let $\pi_k(G)$ denote the number of proper $k$-colourings of $G$. If $p \in \bbz[x]$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients satisfying $p(k) = \pi_k(G)$ for every natural number $k$, then the coefficient of $x^{\nu - 1}$ in $p$ equals $-\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients
